Hi Remy — thanks for the MT103 stub, that helps.

Short answers up front:
- Preferred default for customer payments is SHA (shared). We do not expect to automatically absorb intermediary fees.
- If the payer agrees to set CHARGES=OUR, Redwood will accept the payment gross and not seek a reimbursement. If payer cannot (or refuses), we ask that the payer leave SHA and we will add a reimbursable line for the fee on the next invoice (or issue a small supplemental invoice) to recover the shortfall.

Routing/field guidance to pass to the payer (helps avoid intermediary deductions):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd / IBAN: GB29NWBK60161331926819 (example EUR IBAN)
- Beneficiary Bank: National Europe Bank (BIC: NEBEGB2LXXX)
- If instructing via USD correspondent, set Correspondent/Intermediary to: CHASUS33XXX (JP Morgan Chase, NYC) / Account: 123456789 (use exact account if payer bank requires).
- SWIFT tags example to include in payment instruction or MT103 narrative:
  - :50K: PAYER NAME / PAYER ADDRESS
  - :56A: CHASUS33XXX (correspondent)
  - :57A: NEBEGB2LXXX (beneficiary bank)
  - :59: /GB29NWBK60161331926819
  - /REMI/ INV-20260731 / Redwood Inference Ltd

Charges option implications:
- OUR — payer pays all fees (beneficiary receives full gross amount). This is simplest for Redwood but sometimes resisted by customers.
- SHA — fees split. The payer's bank likely deducts intermediary fees before credit and your ERP will show a short payment; Redwood will then invoice the shortfall as a reimbursable expense.
- BEN — beneficiary absorbs all fees (not acceptable for Redwood unless contractually agreed).

VAT/tax treatment guidance (high level — share with your tax team):
- For cross-border B2B services (EU company paying a non-EU provider like Redwood US/UK entity), the general rule is reverse-charge applies — services/fees typically not charged VAT if we have the customer's valid VAT ID.
- Intermediary bank fees are usually a pass-through (reimbursable bank charges). How they are treated for VAT can vary by member state; in many cases they are out-of-scope or not subject to VAT when billed as a direct reimbursement. To be safe we recommend:
  - Include the bank/intermediary fee as a separate reimbursable line item on the invoice (currency and amount in USD), with a short note: "Reimbursable intermediary bank charges incurred on collection."
  - If customer provides EU VAT ID and the supply is B2B, show VAT as 0% with "reverse charge" wording on the invoice.
  - If you need Redwood to show VAT on the reimbursed fee (rare), escalate to our tax team — we can run a quick country-specific check.

Next steps (proposed):
1) If payer can resend with CHARGES=OUR and include the SWIFT tags above, we will accept the payment as final.
2) If payer keeps SHA, please confirm the exact shortfall amount and we will add a reimbursable line to the next invoice (or issue INV-20260731-ADJ).
3) Please confirm payer's VAT ID (if EU). With that we will mark invoice as reverse-charge.

I attached a sample remittance snippet (swift_message_stub.txt) and a suggested invoice layout we can reissue. If you want us to prepare the updated invoice now with a reimbursable line so you can approve, say the word and we'll push it out.
